title: Errands
goal: Get things done around town: take out cash, sort out a SIM or a broken phone, get clothes stitched or ironed, get a haircut and send a parcel.
intro:
Life in Bhubaneswar or Cuttack is full of small errands: a queue at the bank, a cracked screen, a blouse at the tailor's, a haircut, a parcel to send home. This unit gives you the words for all of them — many of them English words that Odia has made its own (ଏଟିଏମ୍, ସିମ୍, ରିଚାର୍ଜ, କୁରିଅର୍).

The key grammar is the **causative**: Odia turns *do* into *get done* by adding **-ଆଇ-** to the verb — କରିବା 'do' → **କରାଇବା** 'get (it) done', କାଟିବା 'cut' → **କଟାଇବା** 'get (it) cut'. You'll also learn how to say *it'll be ready*, *it got stuck* and *how long will it take?* without saying who does the work.

vocab.note: With endings the hasanta is usually dropped: ଏଟିଏମରୁ eṭiemru "from the ATM".
The formal Odia word is ଖାତା, but at the bank everyone says ଆକାଉଣ୍ଟ.
ଟଙ୍କା କାଢ଼ିବା "to withdraw money". Past: କାଢ଼ିଲି.

ଆଧାର କାର୍ଡ "Aadhaar (ID) card", ଏଟିଏମ୍ କାର୍ଡ "debit card".

ଦସ୍ତଖତ କରିବା "to sign". Also heard: ସାଇନ୍ କରିବା.
From the brand Xerox; ଫଟୋକପି is also used. ଜେରକ୍ସ କରାଇବା "to get a photocopy made".
Usually ସିମ୍ କାର୍ଡ or just ସିମ୍. You need an ID (ଆଧାର କାର୍ଡ) to get one.
ରିଚାର୍ଜ କରିବା "to top up"; ରିଚାର୍ଜ ହୋଇଗଲା "the recharge went through".

ମରାମତି କରିବା "to repair" — on signboards and in careful speech. In the shop people mostly say ଠିକ୍ କରିବା or ରିପେୟାର କରିବା.

vocab.en: to get (something) done; to have someone do

ମୁଁ ନିଜେ କରିବି "I'll do it myself". ନିଜର "one's own".
ଇସ୍ତ୍ରି କରିବା "to iron". The man with a charcoal iron at the street corner is the ଇସ୍ତ୍ରିବାଲା.
ସିଲେଇ କରିବା "to stitch", ସିଲେଇ କରାଇବା "to get stitched".
ମାପ ନେବା "to take measurements", ମାପ ଦେବା "to give (have) your measurements (taken)".
For "tight" people mostly use English ଟାଇଟ୍ (ṭaiṭ).
Almost always made to measure by a tailor.
From "saloon". The traditional barber is the ବାରିକ; for women's salons people say ପାର୍ଲର୍ (parlôr).
ଚୁଟି କଟାଇବା "to get a haircut". ବାଳ (baḷô) is hair in general, including body hair.
ଦାଢ଼ି କାଟିବା "to shave", ଦାଢ଼ି ରଖିବା "to grow a beard".
Causative କଟାଇବା "to get cut": ମୁଁ ଚୁଟି କଟାଇଲି "I got a haircut".
Washing by hand at home is still common; the traditional washerman is the ଧୋବା.
କୁରିଅର୍ କରିବା "to send by courier".
In a restaurant ପାର୍ସଲ୍ means takeaway: ପାର୍ସଲ୍ କରିଦିଅନ୍ତୁ "pack it to take away".
Short for ମେଡିକାଲ ଦୋକାନ; the formal word is ଔଷଧ ଦୋକାନ.

grammar.title: Getting things done: the causative -ଆଇବା
grammar.body:
When someone *else* does the work for you — the tailor stitches, the barber cuts, the shop photocopies — Odia uses a **causative** verb. You make it by putting **-ଆଇ-** between the stem and the ending (the stem vowel sometimes changes):

କରିବା *kôriba* 'do' → **କରାଇବା** *kôraiba* 'get done'
କାଟିବା *kaṭiba* 'cut' → **କଟାଇବା** *kôṭaiba* 'get cut'
ଧୋଇବା *dhoiba* 'wash' → **ଧୁଆଇବା** *dhuaiba* 'get washed'
ଲେଖିବା *lekhiba* 'write' → **ଲେଖାଇବା** *lekhaiba* 'have written'
ଖାଇବା *khaiba* 'eat' → **ଖୁଆଇବା** *khuaiba* 'feed'

You already know two of these: ଦେଖାଇବା 'show' (make see) and ଶିଖାଇବା 'teach' (make learn).

With the many **noun + କରିବା** verbs, just change କରିବା to **କରାଇବା**: ଠିକ୍ କରାଇବା 'get fixed', ସିଲେଇ କରାଇବା 'get stitched', ଇସ୍ତ୍ରି କରାଇବା 'get ironed', ଜେରକ୍ସ କରାଇବା 'get photocopied'.

The endings are the regular ones on the stem **କରା-**: ମୁଁ କରାଏ (I get it done, habitually) · କରାଉଛି (I'm getting it done) · କରାଇଲି (I got it done) · କରାଇଛି (I've had it done) · କରାଇବି (I'll get it done) · ତୁମେ କରାଅ / କରାଇଲ · ଆପଣ କରାନ୍ତି / କରାଇଲେ.

**Who does the job**: put the place or person with **ପାଖରେ** ('at X's'): ଦରଜି ପାଖରେ ସିଲେଇ କରାଇଲି 'I had it stitched at the tailor's'. To say you sent someone to do it, use **-କୁ ଦେଇ** ('through'): ପୁଅକୁ ଦେଇ ଫର୍ମ ଜମା କରାଇଲେ 'she had her son hand in the form'.

**The trap**: ମୁଁ ଜାମା ଧୋଇଲି means *I* washed the shirt; ମୁଁ ଜାମା ଧୁଆଇଲି means I *had* it washed. In relaxed speech people do say ଚୁଟି କାଟିଲି for 'I got a haircut' (as English says 'I cut my hair'), but with ନିଜେ 'myself' the difference matters: ନିଜେ କାଟିଲି = I really did it myself.

grammar.title: It'll be done, it got stuck: ହେବା partners and -ଇଯିବା
grammar.body:
At a counter you often don't care *who* does something, only that it gets done. Odia handles this with verb **pairs**: a *doing* verb with **କରିବା** and a *happening* verb with **ହେବା**:

ଠିକ୍ କରିବା 'fix' — ଠିକ୍ ହେବା 'get fixed'
ଜମା କରିବା 'deposit' — ଜମା ହେବା 'be deposited, be credited'
ଚାର୍ଜ କରିବା 'charge' — ଚାର୍ଜ ହେବା 'be charging'
ବନ୍ଦ କରିବା 'switch off, close' — ବନ୍ଦ ହେବା 'go off, shut'

ମୁଁ ଫୋନ ଠିକ୍ କରିବି 'I'll fix the phone' (the mechanic speaking) but ଫୋନ ଠିକ୍ ହୋଇଯିବ 'the phone will get fixed'.

**-ଇ + ଯିବା**: adding ଯିବା ('go') after the -ଇ form gives a sense of something *happening to* a thing or being *completed*: ହୋଇଯିବ 'it'll get done', ଭାଙ୍ଗିଗଲା 'it broke', ଅଟକିଗଲା 'it got stuck', ମିଳିଯିବ 'you'll get it'. In the past ଯିବା becomes ଗଲା; in the perfect ଯାଇଛି (ଜମା ହୋଇଯାଇଛି 'it has been credited').

**ମିଳିବା 'to be got'** puts the person who receives in the **dative**: ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ କାଲି ମିଳିଯିବ 'you'll get it tomorrow', ମୋତେ ମିଳିନି 'I haven't got it'. Don't say ~~ମୁଁ ମିଳିବି~~ for 'I'll get it' — that means 'I'll be found'!

**ଲାଗିବା for time and cost** (as in unit 23): the time is the subject — ଦୁଇ ଦିନ ଲାଗିବ 'it'll take two days', କେତେ ଲାଗିବ? 'how much / how long will it take?'. Habitual ଲାଗେ: ସାଧାରଣତଃ ଗୋଟିଏ ଦିନ ଲାଗେ 'it usually takes a day'.

culture: Errands in Odisha run on a mix of apps and old-fashioned visits. Phone recharges and bills are paid by UPI, but SIM cards, bank accounts and many forms still need you in person with your **ଆଧାର କାର୍ଡ** and a **ଜେରକ୍ସ** of it — every market has a photocopy shop for exactly this. Address shopkeepers, mechanics and tailors as **ଭାଇ** or **ଭାଇନା** (to a man) and **ଅପା** (to a woman), with ଆପଣ forms; with a young barber or the ironing man (ଇସ୍ତ୍ରିବାଲା) many people slip into ତୁମେ, which is fine if he is younger than you. Polite bargaining is normal at small repair shops (ଟିକେ କମ କରନ୍ତୁ), less so at the bank or a chain store. Saree blouses are still stitched to measure, and the tailor's ‘କାଲି ଆସନ୍ତୁ’ (come tomorrow) before a festival is a running joke — order early before Durga Puja or Raja.

lessons.title: At the bank and the ATM

tip.title: Errand verbs: noun + କରିବା
tip.body:
- Many errand verbs are a noun + **କରିବା**: ଜମା କରିବା 'deposit', ଦସ୍ତଖତ କରିବା 'sign', ରିଚାର୍ଜ କରିବା 'top up'.
- English words slot straight in: ଆକାଉଣ୍ଟ ଖୋଲିବା 'open an account', କାର୍ଡ କାମ କରୁନି 'the card isn't working'.
- 'From the ATM' takes **-ରୁ**: ଏଟିଏମରୁ ଟଙ୍କା କାଢ଼ିବା.

lessons.title: Sorting out your phone

tip.title: Fix it vs. it gets fixed
tip.body:
- Doing verb **ଠିକ୍ କରିବା** 'fix' ↔ happening verb **ଠିକ୍ ହେବା** 'get fixed'.
- Add **ଯିବା** after the -ଇ form for something that happens or gets completed: ଭାଙ୍ଗି**ଗଲା** 'it broke', ହୋଇ**ଯିବ** 'it'll get done'.
- No need to say who does it: ଫୋନ ଠିକ୍ ହୋଇଯିବ.
tip.pattern: ମୁଁ ଠିକ୍ କରିବି · ଫୋନ ଠିକ୍ ହୋଇଯିବ

new: ମୁଁ ଗୋଟିଏ ସିମ୍ କାର୍ଡ ନେବାକୁ ଚାହୁଁଛି।

sentences.en: I can't fix it myself.

tip.title: Do → get done: -ଆଇବା
tip.body:
- Add **-ଆଇ-** to the stem for 'get it done': କରିବା → **କରାଇବା**, କାଟିବା → **କଟାଇବା**, ଧୋଇବା → **ଧୁଆଇବା**.
- Noun + କରିବା verbs just switch to କରାଇବା: ଜେରକ୍ସ **କରାଇବା**, ଇସ୍ତ୍ରି **କରାଇବା**.
- Endings are regular: କରାଏ, କରାଉଛି, କରାଇଲି, କରାଇବି.
- **ନିଜେ କରେ** = I do it myself; **କରାଏ** = I get it done.

tip.title: At X's: ପାଖରେ + causative
tip.body:
- Say *where / by whom* the job is done with **ପାଖରେ**: ଦରଜି **ପାଖରେ** ସିଲେଇ କରାଇଲି 'I had it stitched at the tailor's'.
- Collecting it *from* there is **ପାଖରୁ**: ଦରଜି ପାଖରୁ ଆଣିବି.
- 'Needs doing' = **-ଆଇବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ**: ଛୋଟ କରାଇବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଦରଜି ପାଖରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ପ୍ୟାଣ୍ଟ ସିଲେଇ କରାଉଛି।

sentences.native: ବୋଉ ଦରଜି ପାଖରେ ବ୍ଲାଉଜ୍ ସିଲେଇ କରାଇଲେ।

tip.title: କାଟିବା or କଟାଇବା?
tip.body:
- **କାଟିବା** = cut (you do it); **କଟାଇବା** = get it cut (someone else does).
- The barber asks ଚୁଟି କେମିତି **କାଟିବି**? — you say ମୁଁ ଚୁଟି **କଟାଇବି**.
- Habitual: ମୁଁ **କଟାଏ**, ତୁମେ **କଟାଅ**, ଆପଣ / ସେମାନେ **କଟାନ୍ତି**.
tip.pattern: ମୁଁ କାଟେ (I cut) · ମୁଁ କଟାଏ (I get it cut)

tip.title: How long? ଲାଗିବା and ମିଳିବା
tip.body:
- Time or cost is the subject of **ଲାଗିବା**: ତିନି ଦିନ **ଲାଗିବ** 'it'll take three days'; usually: **ଲାଗେ**.
- **ମିଳିବା** 'be got' puts the receiver in the dative: **ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ** କାଲି ମିଳିଯିବ 'you'll get it tomorrow'.
- Not ~~ମୁଁ ମିଳିବି~~ — that means 'I'll be found'.

sentences.native: ଦିଲ୍ଲୀକୁ କୁରିଅର୍ ଯିବାକୁ ତିନି ଦିନ ଲାଗିବ।
sentences.roman: Dilliku kuriôr jibaku tini dinô lagibô.
sentences.en: A courier to Delhi will take three days.

sentences.native: ପାର୍ସଲ୍ କାଲି ସୁଦ୍ଧା ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ ମିଳିଯିବ।
sentences.roman: parsôl kali suddha apôṇôṅku miḷijibô.

sentences.native: ମୋତେ ମୋ ପାର୍ସଲ୍ ଏପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ମିଳିନି।

sentences.roman: lôṇḍrire luga dhuaibaku kete dinô lage?

sentences.native: ସାଧାରଣତଃ ଦୁଇ ଦିନ ଲାଗେ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଆଜି ଦେଲେ କାଲି ମିଳିଯିବ।

sentences.native: ମେଡିକାଲ ଦୋକାନ ରାତି ଦଶଟା ଯାଏ ଖୋଲା ରହେ।
